title: Event-driven Fabric orchestration
purpose: Events enter through governed streaming connectors, are shaped and evaluated, trigger a bounded Copy job, and close the loop with run telemetry and replay handling.
accessibleSummary: Event-driven Fabric orchestration. Operational event sources; Eventstream routing; Activator condition; Governed Copy job; Telemetry, dedupe and replay.
longDescription: Events enter through governed streaming connectors, are shaped and evaluated, trigger a bounded Copy job, and close the loop with run telemetry and replay handling.

nodes.label: Operational event sources
nodes.summary: Cloud, Kafka, MQTT, database CDC, and Fabric item events provide change signals.
nodes.detail: A source event should identify a business change, not merely replace a frequent polling tick.
nodes.whyItMatters: Good event contracts carry identity and time for deduplication and replay.

evidence.note: Real-Time hub catalogs streams and Fabric or Azure events for event-driven workloads.
Eventstream includes production connectors for Kafka and private-network sources.

drill.example: A file-created event identifies a new supplier extract.
failureModes: Duplicate or out-of-order events trigger repeated work.

nodes.label: Eventstream routing
nodes.summary: Eventstream filters, transforms, deduplicates, and routes events to multiple destinations.
nodes.detail: The stream layer normalizes the signal before automation consumes it.
nodes.whyItMatters: Early shaping keeps downstream rules simple and observable.

evidence.note: Eventstreams provide filtering, cleansing, windowing, deduplication and content-based routing.

drill.example: Only completed-file events for the production path pass to automation.
failureModes: An over-broad filter floods downstream actions.

nodes.label: Activator condition
nodes.summary: Activator continuously evaluates a defined event or metric condition.
nodes.detail: When the condition is met it invokes the configured action instead of waiting for a schedule.
nodes.whyItMatters: The rule is the explicit bridge between detection and work.

evidence.note: Activator can monitor file, table, or metric conditions and invoke a Copy job only when the condition is met.

drill.example: A new production file invokes the supplier Copy job.
failureModes: A noisy rule triggers duplicate executions.

nodes.label: Governed Copy job
nodes.summary: The Copy job moves full or incremental data using configured source, destination, and mappings.
nodes.detail: The action is authored and tested before Activator invokes it.
nodes.whyItMatters: Separating detection from movement keeps retries bounded and auditable.

evidence.note: The recommended pattern defines the Copy job first, then uses an Activator rule to invoke it.

drill.example: The job incrementally loads the new supplier file to bronze.
failureModes: The copy succeeds but its watermark is not committed.

nodes.label: Telemetry, dedupe and replay
nodes.summary: Run history and event identity determine whether to acknowledge, retry, quarantine, or replay.
nodes.detail: Operators reconcile source events with action and Copy job outcomes.
nodes.whyItMatters: The feedback path makes event-driven automation recoverable rather than fire-and-forget.

evidence.note: Operational telemetry over lakehouse workloads is needed to surface failures and maintenance state.

drill.example: A failed copy is replayed once using the same event id after the destination recovers.
failureModes: No correlation exists between event and copy run.
